entertainment.body:
“Wheel of Fortune” got a little more physical than usual when host Ryan Seacrest showed off his yoga moves while opening up about the latest step in his fitness journey.

“I’m not so good. I just started,” the on-air personality, 51, admitted during Wednesday’s episode. “But I have this mat in the office upstairs. Between our meetings, I like to get down and do some things.”

When co-host Vanna White, 69, challenged him to “show” her something, Seacrest was more than happy to demonstrate a few of his newfound moves.

He even dropped into cobra pose, lying on his stomach and pressing his palms into the floor to lift his chest and arch his back.

He then moved into pigeon pose, stretching one leg out behind him while bending the other in front of his body to help open up his hips.

The longtime “American Idol” host said he’s hoping yoga will help him maintain his mobility as he gets older, explaining, “I feel like it’s important that at my age I try to stretch it out.”

He confessed that he’s only taken two yoga classes so far and is still learning the names of the various poses.

“This is my cobra. This is my other insect. I’m not quite sure the names of them yet,” he joked.

entertainment.body:
Chris Brown has agreed to temporarily boost his child support payments to his ex Diamond Brown amid a bitter legal battle over their four-year-old daughter, Lovely.

In legal filings obtained by Billboard , the star singer agreed Wednesday (Nov. 18) to pay $12,000 per month in child support, as well as continue paying other non-cash support — at least until a big hearing next month that his lawyers say could potentially resolve the entire dispute.

The new figure represents a hefty increase from the $7,000 her lawyers say Breezy was previously paying in child support. He has also agreed to pay $25,000 to retroactively cover support back to July and has advanced her $55,000 to cover her legal bills, per the filings.

Brown and Diamond, who split up in 2024, have been in a nasty fight since February, when she accused him on social media of threatening her current boyfriend. She went to court in May, suing him for child support and physical custody.

Brown has opposed her request for sole custody, and the pair have since exchanged bruising statements on social media — including Chris saying he already pays for “everything” even though he hasn’t seen Lovely since March. Diamond fired back that she had offered visits but Chris hadn’t shown: “If you wanted to see your daughter, you would.”

The dispute in court has been no nicer. Last month, she claimed in court filings that Brown had “made death threats against my most recent boyfriend.” In another filing, she said Brown makes between $5.5 and $7.3 million per month and requested he pay roughly $45,000 per month in total support payments to her and their daughter.

Throughout the dispute, C. Breezy has been on the road for his expansive R&B Tour with Usher , which heads to New Orleans this week and will wrap up next month. On the music front, CB released his Brown album in May, which debuted at No. 7 on the Billboard 200.

entertainment.title: A “Very Human” Father-Daughter Story: ‘THR Presents’ Q&A With Myrsini Aristidou on Cyprus’ First Oscar Submission, ‘Hold Onto Me’
entertainment.summary: The director of Sundance audience winner on casting a first-time actress, shooting a night scene in a freezing sea and her films’ love stories.
entertainment.body:
Cyprus has submitted its first-ever international feature film Oscar contender: Hold Onto Me , the feature debut of writer-director Myrsini Aristidou.

The film, starring newcomer Maria Petrova and Christos Passalis ( Dogtooth ), premiered at Sundance, where it won the World Cinema Dramatic Audience Award. It follows Iris, 11, whose grandfather has died, which leads to petty criminal Aris — the father she has never known — arriving in town. Can what starts out as a stubborn attempt to connect develop into a fragile bond? Related Stories Movies The Free World Award Is Made From Weapons Metal. The First Winner: Iraq's Oscar Entry Movies "Hollywood Rewrites History" and Calls for Authentic Female Characters: Tallinn Debates Cinema Amid Global Crisis

Hold Onto Me is a Cyprus-Denmark-Greece co-production that takes a deep dive into a beach community and is partially inspired by the filmmaker’s personal experience. During a taping of THR Presents , Aristidou shared how “the narrative arc of all my films is sort of a love story and the disappointments that come with it.”

Hold Onto Me is based in Cyprus, but addresses universal themes. How would you describe what the film explores? And how important was it for you to show us characters who are not fully good or bad?

The subject matter is something that I care about a lot — all of us [do], I think. Our relationship with our parents matters. It is something we carry with us. We either work on it to improve it or make it better or heal it — or many people let it go as well and just move on and try not to repeat the same patterns. …

I care a lot about characters that are real, that are very imperfect, very human in their own way, and maybe even lonely in many ways.

She had never done acting before, actually. Our casting director found her in Cyprus. She was younger than what I had written in the script. I wrote the script for a 15-year-old, and she was 10 and a half at the time. Yet, there was something about her. There was this innocence and authenticity. There is an emergency scene in the sea. I don’t imagine you had a big water tank that you filmed in?

It was very, very different and complicated. We didn’t have the budget to shoot in a pool. We shot in the sea. It was very cold; we shot at night. … We were splashing water with our hands.

entertainment.title: ‘The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth’ Review: Brad Pitt, David Fincher and Quentin Tarantino Mix a Cool Cocktail in Free-Flowing Spinoff
entertainment.summary: Elizabeth Debicki, Scott Caan, Carla Gugino and Yahya Abdul-Mateen II also star in Netflix’s paean to late ‘70s Los Angeles, which revisits the stuntman from ‘Once Upon a Time in Hollywood.’
entertainment.body:
It’s difficult to imagine a song choice more precisely capturing the essence of a movie than Boz Scaggs’ mellow yacht rock groove “Lowdown,” which kicks off the end credits of The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth . That might seem odd for a gritty comedy that builds to an ultraviolent climactic bloodbath, but this standalone chapter in the life of the now-retired stuntman from Once Upon a Time in Hollywood — the role that won Brad Pitt an Oscar — saunters along to its own idiosyncratic beat, running on a well-lubricated R&B engine.

The star’s golden glow and loose-limbed charisma, David Fincher ’s exactingly controlled direction and the shaggier storytelling style of Quentin Tarantino ’s screenplay are not always the most seamless fit. But the obvious mutual esteem and affection shared by that creative triumvirate is contagious and the movie has a good-time vibe that just won’t quit — even if it feels more stretched and less substantive than its 2019 predecessor. Still, few fans will complain, especially those who opt for the IMAX experience, before it hits Netflix on Dec. 23. Related Stories Movies Ron Howard Wasn't Sure He Was the Right Director for 'Avedon'; This Is What Changed His Mind TV Netflix to Adapt 'Grendel' Comic Books Into Adult Animated TV Series The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth The Bottom Line Sexy, seductive and chaotic in mostly fun ways. Release date : Weds., Nov. 25 (in theaters); Weds., Dec. 23 (streaming) Cast : Brad Pitt, Elizabeth Debicki, Scott Caan, Carla Gugino, Yahya Abdul-Mateen II, Peter Weller, Matt Groove, JB Tadena, Corey Fogelmanis, Karren Karagulian, Lauren Glazier, Timothy Olyphant, Nicholas Hammond Director : David Fincher Screenwriter : Quentin Tarantino Rated R, 2 hours 23 minutes

Eight years have passed since Cliff and Leonardo DiCaprio’s faded TV star Rick Dalton, for whom Pitt’s character worked as a longtime stunt double, mopped up three homicidal Manson followers — described here as “those fuckin’ hippie intruders” — in pools of their own blood. Rick is now starring in a TV series in Australia drolly titled Dingo Dan , and Cliff has aged out of the stunt game, though his is not an idle retirement.

He works as a projectionist at the New Beverly Cinema — the historic repertory house in the Fairfax district now owned and programmed by Tarantino as a 35mm stronghold — where the fictional blaxploitation film Soul Brothers Die Hard has been such a hit that Cliff can recite the dialogue along with the actors. Its cast is topped by former Oakland Raiders player Roderick “Hot Rod” Harrison ( Yahya Abdul-Mateen II ), who opens Fincher’s film with a quintessential Tarantino provocation, enlightening his character’s nephew about “how to keep multiple bitches turnt out.”

entertainment.title: It Girl India Amarteifo’s Queen’s Gambit
entertainment.summary: The 25-year-old actress followed her 'Bridgerton' breakthrough with a long, thoughtful pause. Now she’s making her move with ‘Clarissa.’
entertainment.body:
India Amarteifio went to bed on May 3, 2023, a working but largely unknown young actress. The next morning — after Netflix dropped Queen Charlotte : A Bridgerton Story , a prequel in which Amarteifio plays a younger version of Golda Rosheuvel’s imperious royal — she woke up famous.

“The first thing I did that day was walk down the street with my co-star Corey [Mylchreest], and we were immediately recognized and stopped by fans,” she says. “We just looked at each other like, ‘OK, life has changed now.’ ”

Three years later, Amarteifio, 25, is still getting stopped on the street — at least three or four times a day. “People still rewatch it, or a new Bridgerton comes out and puts the spotlight back on,” she says. “I do wonder whether I’m going to be Queen Charlotte forever.” Related Stories Movies A "Very Human" Father-Daughter Story: 'THR Presents' Q&A With Myrsini Aristidou on Cyprus' First Oscar Submission, 'Hold Onto Me' Movies The Free World Award Is Made From Weapons Metal. The First Winner: Iraq's Oscar Entry

Not a bad problem to have, considering her previous career anxiety: that her days as an actor might already be finished.

“It’s so silly, but I wasn’t booking anything, and I thought, ‘My time has passed at 20 years old,’ ” she says with a laugh.

Then came Queen Charlotte — and literal overnight success. The series instantly hit No. 1 on Netflix, topped Nielsen’s streaming charts and went on to surpass 80 million views, becoming one of the platform’s most popular titles.

After waiting so long for her big break, Amarteifio was willing to wait a little longer for the right follow-up. She took a long pause after Queen Charlotte , thinking about the career she wanted beyond the show that had made her famous. The offers were coming, but she was holding out for “more art house, indie, character-driven” projects.

She found what she was looking for in Clarissa , a Neon film from Nigerian twin filmmakers Arie and Chuko Esiri that opens in select U.S. theaters Dec. 11. Their reimagining of Mrs. Dalloway casts Hotel Rwanda Oscar nominee Sophie Okonedo as a Lagos society woman revisiting the summer that shaped her life, with Amarteifio taking over in the flashbacks. Ayo Edebiri and David Oyelowo round out the cast.

entertainment.body:
Eminem joined forces with Spotify to celebrate the Detroit legend becoming part of the streaming giant’s Billions Club with an episode from the popular series, which arrived on Wednesday (Nov. 18).

In typical Em fashion, he put his own creative spin on the visual, drawing inspiration from his animated The Slim Shady Show from 2000.

In the episode, Eminem appears at the Spotify office surrounded by Billions Club accolades, and then he’s fittingly served a dish of his mom’s spaghetti in the “Lose Yourself” plaque.

The “Not Afraid” rapper gets annoyed when sauce spills on his new Air Jordan 4s, and then an old friend taking on his Slim Shady persona greets him from the center of the pasta dish.

Em is then pulled into an animated world and takes a trip down memory lane while getting quizzed on his classic hits that have joined the Billions Club over the years, including “Not Afraid,” “Stan,” “Lose Yourself,” “Love the Way You Lie” with Rihanna, “Godzilla” featuring Juice WRLD, “Mockingbird,” “Superman,” “Till I Collapse,” “Rap God” and Akon’s “Smack That.”

The episode closes with Em returning to the real world and threatening to kill his Slim Shady alter ego, who’s hiding out in the spaghetti, a callback to his 2024 album, The Death of Slim Shady (Coup de Grâce) , which arrived in July 2024 and topped the Billboard 200.

Eminem has reached the summit of the Billboard Hot 100 on five separate occasions in his decorated career. He reached No. 1 with both of his Rihanna collaborations “Love the Way You Lie” and “The Monster,” as well as “Not Afraid,” “Lose Yourself” and “Crack a Bottle,” the last track with his close friends Dr. Dre and 50 Cent.

50 actually revealed in October that Em is working on a new album, which caused the Detroit rapper to pull out of contributing to the Street Fighter soundtrack. Fif told the Associated Press at the film’s premiere: “Em, he put a couple pieces together for it and decided because he got closer to his album, he kinda fell back on that because he’s preparing his presentation for the next album.”

entertainment.title: Why Kacey Musgraves, Miranda Lambert Song Cut Out at CMA Awards
entertainment.summary: Kacey Musgraves and Miranda Lambert might like to cuss (and smoke and drink) but the CMA Awards had reign them in. During the duo’s rendition of their song “Horses and Divorces” at the CMA Awards...
entertainment.body:
Kacey Musgraves and Miranda Lambert might like to cuss (and smoke and drink) but the CMA Awards had reign them in.

During the duo’s rendition of their song “Horses and Divorces” at the CMA Awards Nov. 18, many country fans noticed that their performance was partially obstructed from the broadcast—and that’s all due to the language in the song.

While some stars opt to perform a clean version of their songs to follow the Federal Communications Commission guidelines, Musgraves and Lambert performed the original lyrics, which sees Lambert sing, “I’ve done my fair share of s--t talkin,’ too.”

Those present at the ceremony in Bridgestone Arena in Nashville were able to hear Lambert’s entire vocals, but during the ABC broadcast, there was a few seconds of white noise that confused viewers—especially those unfamiliar with the duet.

Luckily, the country singers’ hook, “hell just froze over” is permitted by the FCC and it exemplifies just how momentous the song—which is featured on Musgraves’ album Middle of Nowhere —truly is, considering the stars were previously at odds which each other.

Musgraves admitted during an interview with CBS Mornings earlier this year that it was “common knowledge there was a bit of soft tension” between her and Lambert—and so she decided to bury the hatchet once and for all by featuring the “The House that Built Me” singer on her latest album.

Lambert, for her part, shared she was surprised by Musgraves’ request.

“I hadn’t heard from her in a while,” Lambert—who split from Blake Shelton in 2015—explained in a separate interview during the same CBS Mornings segment. “She texted me and was like, ‘I need to ask you something but I need to ask you on the phone, like I want to talk about this.’”

entertainment.title: A Pop-Star Acting Newbie, the Afterlife and “Dirty Energy”: The Making of ‘La Bola Negra’
entertainment.summary: Directing duo Javier Ambrossi and Javier Calvo stretch a love story across the Spanish Civil War, three generations and.the great beyond.
entertainment.body:
Javier Calvo was traveling with his filmmaking partner, Javier Ambrossi, when he read Alberto Conejero’s play La Piedra Oscura ( The Dark Stone ) and the idea for La Bola Negra ( The Black Ball ) took hold. Conejero’s drama, set in a military hospital during the Spanish Civil War, imagines the last night of Rafael Rodríguez Rapún — a Republican lieutenant and the real-life lover of playwright Federico García Lorca — in conversation with Sebastián, the young Nationalist soldier who is to execute him at dawn.

“I imagined this little gay boy having to leave his town, all this tragedy, and how this happened to my country only 90 years ago, and having a gay character in the civil war,” says Calvo. “We never talk about that. Where were we? What happened to us? It hit me, and I started to cry. I told Javi, ‘I think we have to make this.’ ” Related Stories Movies 'Obsession' Breakout Inde Navarrette to Receive Spotlight Tribute at Gotham Film Awards (Exclusive) Movies The Free World Award Is Made From Weapons Metal. The First Winner: Iraq's Oscar Entry

The film, co-written with Conejero, braids three timelines. In 1932 Granada, Carlos (Milo Quifes), a young upper-class Andalusian, is blackballed from an exclusive casino because he’s gay — the premise of Lorca’s unfinished play La Bola Negra , of which only four pages survive. In 1937, Sebastián (singer- songwriter Guitarricadelafuente ) keeps watch over Rafael (Miguel Bernardeau). And in 2017 Madrid, Alberto (Carlos González) learns that he is Sebastián’s grandson. Sebastián has left him the rest of Lorca’s play — pages the film imagines into being — which he had promised Rafael he would save. Those pages — verified by Glenn Close, who plays a Spanish-speaking American scholar named Isabelle Durand — lead Alberto and his relatives to discover that Sebastián spent most of his life secretly living with another man.

“This is a movie about what we pass on to the next generation,” Ambrossi says. “It’s about inheritance.”

The co-directors, known as Los Javis among their collaborators because of their shared first names, reassembled their usual crafts team to begin shaping each timeline: cinematographer Gris Jordana, editor Alberto Gutiérrez, production designer Roger Bellés, costume designer Ana López Cobos, composer Raül Refree and casting directors Eva Leira and Yolanda Serrano.

The directors were already keen on Guitarricadelafuente and Bernardeau for their respective roles, as well as González for the part of Alberto, which Ambrossi calls “a creation.”

entertainment.title: All the Country Stars in Taylor Swift’s CMA Awards Performance, Explained
entertainment.summary: For her first performance in 13 years at the awards show on Wednesday, Swift lined up a score of cameos from her country music past
entertainment.body:
We already knew that when Taylor Swift returned to the CMAs for the first time in 13 years, the night was going to be packed with easter eggs . What we didn’t know was that her performance would be far more than just that, filled with appearances from country stars who have all played an important role in her storied career since it kicked off in Nashville with her self-titled debut in 2006.

Swift began the performance of her nominated song “ I Knew It, I Knew You ” in her dressing room (with outfits from her Taylor Swift era scattered across the room, mind you) before making her way backstage at the Bridgestone Arena en route to the stage. Here, we walk through all the artists she encountered along the way.

As Swift rounded the corner from her dressing room, there he was: Brad Paisley, polishing a handful of CMA Awards . Paisley had already made a surprise appearance earlier in the night to join Lainey Wilson for a musical monologue, but his significance in Swift’s country music story is substantial. Swift opened for Paisley on his Bonfires & Amplifiers Tour in 2007, where he apparently played a prank on the young artist, releasing crickets on her tour bus. “For months, I couldn’t sleep,” Swift said in October when she was inducted into the Nashville Songwriters Hall of Fame. Clearly there’s no, er, bad blood remaining.

Up next in Swift’s stroll were Little Big Town, the foursome of Karen Fairchild, Kimberly Schlapman, Phillip Sweet, and Jimi Westbrook. Little Big Town had a hit in 2016 with a version of Swift’s song “ Better Man, ” which was originally crafted for Red (Swift eventually recorded her own take of the solo write as a vault track). “I’m grateful for her friendship through the years,” Fairchild told Rolling Stone , “and we love her so much. She found her better man.”

Swift did a little dance with Kristian Bush and Jennifer Nettles of Sugarland, a duo with whom she has a longstanding relationship. Swift opened for Sugarland in 2007, and even owns a signed copy of their debut EP, Premium Quality Tunes . A decade later, when Swift was looking for someone to sing a song she’d written, “Babe,” she called up the twosome. They ended up recording it for their album Bigger . Swift also served as a guest on the track, even appearing in the dramatic music video. entertainment.title: Your Favorite THC Drinks Are About to Be Illegal
entertainment.summary: A new law will clamp down on hemp farming, and effectively ban products veterans and others Americans rely on
entertainment.body:
On Tuesday, more than two dozen veterans organizations sent an open letter to bipartisan congressional leaders demanding something that a few years ago might have been unheard of: better access to legal weed. “Veterans have sacrificed for our country, and they deserve safe, responsible options for managing chronic pain, PTSD, anxiety, sleep problems, and other health conditions,” it read. “Many veterans… rely on hemp products as an alternative to opioids. If Congress fails to act, the products they depend on will suddenly become illegal.”

That’s because on Dec. 11, a new law that limits the amount of THC allowed in hemp will go into effect, eradicating the cannabis market as Americans have come to know it. The colorful cans of THC sodas on Trader Joe’s shelves will be gone, as will the sleep-aid gummies from Target and and the bottles of THC “liquor” at Total Wines. “Anyone who produces the seed, grows a crop, processes the crop, makes a product, sells it to the shelf, and the people who buy it — all these people will be impacted,” explains Greg Serrao, co-founder of Willie’s Remedy, one of the country’s best-selling cannabis drinks.

The new definition will close an eight-year loophole that allowed the CBD market to take off, followed by the federally legal THC market. Veterans, farmers, and cannabis entrepreneurs agree that more regulations are needed to help finally wrangle what was, for a long time, a frontier industry. “A lot of people paint this picture of hemp as this wild west,” says Serrao. “That’s not true.”

What is true is that unless Congress acts to amend the new rules, in less than a month, a $28 billion industry will disappear. “Something like 65 percent of our customers are senior citizens, and 70 percent are over 45,” says Willie’s Remedy’s other co-founder, Forrest Dein.

Sens. Tim Sheehy (R-Mont.) and Amy Klobuchar (D-Minn.) introduced a bill to the Senate on Tuesday that would halt the new rules, instead offering a new set of regulations around hemp-derived THC products, including age limits, testing and packaging requirements, and other guardrails around the plant. “Our bill will put every bad actor in the hemp space out of business and keep intoxicating products out of the hands of children,” Sheehy, a veteran, said in a press release. “It will also stop Congress from turning the farmers, veterans, and cancer patients who rely on these products into criminals overnight.” Editor’s picks The 250 Greatest Albums of the 21st Century So Far The 100 Best TV Episodes of All Time The 500 Greatest Albums of All Time 100 Best Movies of the 21st Century

sports.title: Christian Parker considered not staying with the Cowboys
sports.summary: The Cowboys have removed play-calling duties from defensive coordinator Christian Parker.
sports.body:
Parker told reporters on Thursday that he decided to process the “significant” disappointment by remaining in his job, albeit with the most important role taken away.

“That would have been running from it,” Parker said as to the possibility of resigning.

As to whether it will be awkward moving forward, Parker said, “I think it’s only awkward if you make it, and we don’t have to make it that way.”

But it will be awkward. The defensive coordinator isn’t fully coordinating the defense. And it’s not like the situation in Denver, where the head coach assumed the play-calling duties from the coordinator. Parker’s biggest responsibilities were given to someone other than the head coach — a consultant who arrived just last month.

The cleanest approach for the Cowboys, given the team’s obvious lack of confidence in Parker, would have been to fire him. But that would have come with a buyout of the balance of his contract. And owner/G.M. Jerry Jones doesn’t like paying coaches to not work.

Jones likely hopes Parker will eventually realize that the situation isn’t sustainable and (as the lingo goes) “self-select.” That avoids the buyout and conclusively ends the inherently awkward situation.

Mayfield told reporters at a Thursday press conference he hurt the foot while scrambling ahead of a pass to running back Kenneth Gainwell and that he feels he progressed well during the team’s bye week.

Mayfield also said that he feels like he has made enough progress to play against the Lions this weekend, but that decision will ultimately fall on head coach Todd Bowles.

Bowles said earlier this week that a decision would come on Friday, which leaves Mayfield with another day to show he’s good to go on the practice field before any final call about his status is made.

Reich said today that he believes the Jets have enough talent on offense to produce, and he and the coaching staff need to make it happen.

“I’m the offensive coordinator, it starts with me,” Reich said. “I, and we as a staff, have to put the players in position to do what they do. We’ve got a very talented group, so we need to do a better job coaching.”

Over the last nine quarters of play, the Jets have nine Jason Sanders field goals, and no other points. Reich is well aware that three points a quarter isn’t going to win many games.

“Obviously, players need to do their part and execute and make plays,” Reich said. “For all of us, it’s a collective effort. We know we need to put more points on the board, whether it’s in the red zone or whether it’s further out, we still want to be explosive. We need to get back on track there. It’s been nine quarters. Believe me, I feel every play of that nine quarters.”

sports.title: Bill Belichick, Robert Kraft advance to final round of Hall of Fame voting
sports.summary: Belichick and Kraft were also finalists in last year's selection process.
sports.body:
The Hall announced on Thursday that Belichick has been chosen as the nominee in the coach category while Kraft is the nominee in the contributor category. That was also the case last year, but neither of them were elected.

Belichick’s failure to get enough votes for election created a particular outcry given the six Super Bowl titles he won while coaching Kraft’s Patriots from 2000-2023.

The Hall of Fame overhauled selection procedures in the wake of last year’s election. The size of the selection committee was cut in half from 50 to 25 and there is no longer be a separate category for senior players.

Belichick and Kraft will join 13 player nominees for consideration by the committee. That list of candidates will be reduced to seven before a final vote with 80 percent approval needed for election.

sports.title: Deshaun Watson on future with Browns: That's up to my agent, I don't worry about that
sports.summary: After several years marred by poor play and injuries, Deshaun Watson has provided some return on the investment the Browns made with the infamous 2022 trade to acquire him.
sports.body:
Watson has engineered a league-high six game-winning drives for the Browns, who stand at 6-4 and the AFC’s current No. 7 seed.

The five-year commitment the franchise made to him is just about at its end, with 2026 representing the final season of the original deal.

With the team on its bye in Week 11, has Watson thought about an appropriate time to speak with the organization about his future?

“That’s up to my agent. So, that’s all David Mulugheta,” Watson said, via transcript from the team. “I don’t even worry about that, even all the way up to the last game. My future and what that holds is all in God’s hands, and whoever contacts David. Right now, again, it’s just playing good football, winning games, enjoying this moment, because it can all be taken away regardless. Right now, I’m just focusing on today, this bye week, and then getting back up here and finishing out the season strong for us.”

Asked as a follow-up if he’s opened the door for his agent to speak with the Browns about the future, Watson again sidestepped.

“Yeah, that’s a David question,” Watson said. “That’s my agent, I’m going to leave that up to my agent for sure.”

While the Browns have gone 6-3 with Watson as a starter so far in 2026, the quarterback’s numbers are not overwhelming. He’s completed 65.1 percent of his passes for 2,118 yards with seven touchdowns and four interceptions — good for an 89.1 passer rating. He’s also taken a league-high 37 sacks.

At 3-6, time is running out for the Texans. If they can’t beat the Colts at home, the Texans have no shot at pulling themselves back into the race for a wild-card berth.

Buffalo has a rough stretch coming. This is the worst time to step into a trap. Fortunately, the Dolphins may not be talented enough to take advantage of the opportunity to catch the Bills napping.

sports.title: Bears-Lions Thanksgiving audience will be huge — and it could have been even bigger
sports.summary: Last year, both of the early Thanksgiving Day games broke the prior record for NFL regular-season audience size.
sports.body:
With one small tweak to the schedule, it perhaps wouldn’t be.

In 2025, Packers-Lions attracted an incredible 47.7 million viewers. This year, the looming battle between the 7-2 Bears and 7-2 Lions should approach (if not match . . . if not beat) that number.

The problem is the second game. The 2-7 Eagles are in soft-tank mode. The 4-6 Cowboys have disintegrated into defensive disarray. While it will still attract a very large audience given the captive audience and the usual Thanksgiving routines, it likely won’t approach 50 million.

While the NFL has granted a permanent hammerlock to the Lions and Cowboys for the traditional Thanksgiving afternoon games, a simple tweak would have set the stage for Bears-Lions to break 50 million — and perhaps to threaten last year’s record.

Here’s the idea. Why not install flexibility to flip the start times of the afternoon games?

It’s no different than the usual Sunday-afternoon flex, like the one that happened this weekend when Steelers-Eagles moved from 4:25 p.m. ET to 1:00 p.m. ET and Jaguars-Giants slid to the higher-profile slot.

On Thanksgiving, the late-afternoon game always does better than the early one. In some years, the Lions game could be viewed as more attractive than the Cowboys game. This year would be one of those years.

It’s something to consider. Getting an annual Thanksgiving Day game doesn’t mean owning the window. And given the NFL’s current willingness, on and after Week 12, to flex from Sunday to Thursday or Sunday to Monday, why not reserve the right to acknowledge that, for the two afternoon games on Thanksgiving, the “best” one should be played in the higher-profile slot?

sports.title: Mexico City altitude will affect the kicking game on Sunday night
sports.summary: When the Vikings and 49ers face off in Mexico City on Sunday night, they'll be playing at the highest elevation any NFL game is ever played at: Estadio Azteca's altitude is around 7,300 feet.
sports.body:
Kickers and physicists alike have agreed that high altitudes can easily add five yards or more to field goal range. The air is thinner at altitude, and in Mexico City the altitude makes the air about 20 percent less dense than at sea level. In Denver, which is about 2,000 feet lower than Mexico City, the air is about 15 percent less dense than at sea level, and Denver’s Mile High Stadium is well known for the boost it gives to kickers.

Vikings kicker Will Reichard has a career-long field goal of 62 yards, and 49ers kicker Eddy Pineiro’s career long is 59 yards. Both kickers made their career longs at sea level, and they both should feel confident if called upon to attempt a kick from at least a few yards beyond 60 yards in Sunday night.

Kickoff strategy may also be a factor at altitude. Only 16 percent of all kickoffs in the NFL this season have gone for touchbacks, as teams believe it’s better to try to pin their opponents deep on their own end of the field than boot the ball into the end zone. In Mexico City, it may be hard for a kicker to avoid kicking the ball into the end zone — or kickers might be able to get a higher trajectory on their kicks and make it even easier to pin their opponents deep.

And punts will travel several yards farther, which could be especially exciting for Vikings return man Myles Price, the NFL’s top punt returner , who might be able to reach top speed before the coverage can get to him if 49ers punter Corliss Waitman outkicks his coverage.

There’s a lot of talk before games at altitude about how teams should acclimate so their players don’t get out of breath in the thinner air. But that’s not the only part of the game that players will need to adjust to on Sunday night. The kicking game will be significantly impacted.

sports.body: Josh Allen is universally regarded as an elite NFL quarterback, but that doesn’t mean he’s immune to criticism. And when Allen criticism arises, it tends to be centered around his interceptions. From his breakout 2020 campaign through 2023, Allen reached double digits in the interception category each year. After only six in 2024’s MVP season, Allen tossed 10 a season ago and already has seven in nine games in 2026. If obtaining a doctoral in football analysis was possible, I would write my dissertation on why we can’t view interceptions in a vacuum and their presence as a necessary byproduct of properly aggressive quarterback play. And a lot more things to challenge conventional wisdom about picks from a quarterback in the NFL. That is not the objective of this article. But it’s related to that. The point here is to demonstrate how Allen’s interceptions are unique. He’s become a master of the arm-punt pick, a worst-case result on a play in which a seismic chance is made in search of a hugely positive play for the offense. And the worst-case result of the arm punt is the least damaging in the grand scheme of all possible interceptions. Shoutout to WGR 550’s Jeremy White for noticing / highlighting this trend a while ago, by the way. Since 2020, Allen has lost an average of 3.76 Expected Points Added on interceptions, the third-lowest average among qualifying quarterbacks. sports.title: Myles Price, NFL's top punt returner, shows he can make an impact on Vikings' offense, too
sports.summary: The Vikings have a big weapon on special teams in return man Myles Price, who is leading the league in punt return average, total yards and touchdowns, and is third in the league in both kickoff return average and total yards.
sports.body:
In the Vikings’ win over the Packers, Price got a career-high 33 snaps on offense, and he responded by catching four passes, including the first touchdown of the game on a 38-yard pass from Kirk Cousins. Vikings head coach Kevin O’Connell told Paul Allen that the decision to give Price so much playing time was mostly because of injuries to starting receivers Jordan Addison and Jauan Jennings, but with the way Price performed, he’ll get more playing time on offense going forward.

“We want to continue to find ways to get Myles involved in the offense,” O’Connell said.

O’Connell said that when the Vikings are as thin at wide receiver as they were on Sunday, there are concerns about getting anyone else injured, and he was worried about seeing Price take hits in the return game.

“With all the injuries the other day, we had no way of getting another player up,” O’Connell said. “There was not another body to have, so we actually went into the game for the first time since I’ve been here with four receivers up. Every time Myles returned a ball, you felt like we could be out of 11 personnel altogether here on one play. He did get banged up a couple times, we tried to feature the bigger groupings, and luckily he was able to return.”

Ultimately, O’Connell believes that when Price has the ball in his hands in the open field, he can make big plays whether on offense or special teams.

“Myles is a guy that we feel very strongly about making that last move, making that last man miss, and being able to score,” O’Connell said.

Expect to see Price do more of that for the rest of the season.

Currently, Burrow and Peyton Manning are tied for the record, with five consecutive four-touchdown games. Manning did it in 2004 with the Colts. Burrow’s last five games have featured:

Three touchdown passes and one touchdown run in a 34-17 win over the Falcons.

Five touchdown passes and one touchdown run in a 43-36 win over the Titans.

Burrow is the MVP favorite , and with 2,795 yards and 27 touchdown passes through nine games this season, he’s closing in on 3,000 yards and 30 touchdowns, which only four quarterbacks have done within their first 10 games of a season: Tom Brady in 2007, Aaron Rodgers in 2011, Manning in 2013 and 2014, and Patrick Mahomes in 2018. That’s good company for a quarterback to be in, and Burrow is playing right now at a level few quarterbacks have ever reached.

sports.title: Kyle Shanahan on the Brian Flores defense: "It's not just a fad"
sports.summary: 49ers coach says the Minnesota defense puts pressure on everyone involved.
sports.body:
They meet again on Sunday night in Mexico City, when Shanahan’s 49ers play the Vikings, whose defense is coordinated by Flores.

“He’s more unique than all the other 31 guys,” Shanahan told reporters on Wednesday regarding Flores. “He’s the one guy who commits to this and it’s not just a fad for these nine games or whatever. He’s been doing it his whole time in Minnesota. He did the same thing in Miami. He’s as good as it gets at that stuff.

“Anybody who lives in that world as much as he does, it’s usually a matter of time. I think offensive coaches used to like to say that early on, but it’s too many years of it and it’s too many games in this year that they’re sound. They put so much pressure on the quarterback, the play-caller, the O-Line, the receivers, on everybody. A lot of times when you go into an NFL game, the pressure’s really on people on third down and stuff like that because those are things where everything can come and when you play against Brian it’s 70-straight plays of that.”

It’s not easy to beat in part because it’s almost impossible to simulate in practice. As Devin McCourty has said, you think you have a plan and then the game starts and everything changes.

It changes in part because Flores seems to be constantly self-scouting and adjusting, defying the films to create pressure in new ways.

The goal is to eliminate the offense’s built-in advantage that comes from knowing what the play will be by creating confusion for the entire offense. Who’s rushing? Who’s dropping into coverage? Who do I block? If that guy doesn’t rush, what do I do?

It makes for a compelling chess match, with the 49ers needing to find a way to get the Minnesota defense on its heels.

A strong running game is a must. Wearing down the defense physically is required. When inevitable passing situations arise, the quarterback needs to quickly find the open man (if there is one) and get the ball out before the walls close in.

The 8-1 Buffalo Bills remain one of the most talk-about teams in the NFL this season. sports.title: Brian Schottenheimer: Christian Parker still has a bright future with the Cowboys
sports.summary: Brian Schottenheimer confirmed Mike Pettine will take over as the Cowboys' defensive play-caller on Sunday.
sports.body:
“Christian Parker is a huge part of what we’re trying to build here and that he is our defensive coordinator,” Schottenheimer said Wednesday, via Todd Archer of ESPN. “He is our leader. He is not changing any of those things, but I do feel that in the best interest of winning that Pet’s calling the game is going to help us get to where we want to get to.”

Schottenheimer said Parker would continue running meetings and leading walkthroughs, but the Cowboys needed “a different perspective” on game day.

Parker, 34, arrived in January as a first-time play caller, leaving Philadelphia after two seasons as the Eagles’ defensive passing game coordinator. The Cowboys, though, rank last in yards (393.8), last in run defense (154.1) and last in third-down defense (48.8 percent). They are 30th in scoring (28.2).

Pettine arrived before Week 5 as a senior defensive assistant to help Parker, whom he brought into the NFL with the Packers in 2019. He was defensive coordinator with the Jets, when Schottenheimer was on staff, and also served in that role with the Bills and Packers.

“When I look at this situation, we’re all committed to trying to get it right,” Schottenheimer said, “and so we’re making adjustments like we’ve made. We’ve made adjustments. We’ve adjusted some scheme. We’ve adjusted some personnel. We’ve adjusted some play time. This is just another adjustment where we’re trying to get right.”

Schottenheimer made clear several times that he still believes in Parker and still believes Parker has a future with the Cowboys.

“CP has a very, very bright future as a coach, but more specifically, a very bright future here as our defense coordinator,” Schottenheimer said.

sports.summary: The Buffalo Bills improved their position in the AFC East with a 31-12 victory over the New York Jets at MetLife Stadium on Sunday Buffalo’s offense played just 57 snaps compared to 71 for the defense. The Jets held a 32:01 to 27:59 advantage in time of possession, but Buffalo made its opportunities
sports.body: The Buffalo Bills improved their position in the AFC East with a 31-12 victory over the New York Jets at MetLife Stadium on Sunday Buffalo’s offense played just 57 snaps compared to 71 for the defense. The Jets held a 32:01 to 27:59 advantage in time of possession, but Buffalo made its opportunities count, producing 389 total yards and four touchdowns. While the Jets finished with a 32:01 to 27:59 advantage in time of possession, that statistic doesn’t tell the entire story. Buffalo actually controlled the clock in the first half, holding the ball for 18:36 compared to New York’s 11:24. The second half was a different story, largely because the Bills’ offense simply didn’t need much time to score. Buffalo produced three touchdown drives totaling just seven offensive plays and 2:49 of possession. Josh Allen capped a four-play drive with a rushing touchdown, connected with DJ Moore on a 45-yard score during a two-play possession, and James Cook put the game away with a 74-yard touchdown run on the first play of another drive. Those three possessions accounted for 21 points in less than three minutes. The defense certainly had its share of extended drives to contend with, but Buffalo’s explosive offensive production played a significant role in the disparity between offensive and defensive snap counts. Offensive snap counts The Bills’ offensive line remained relatively consistent throughout the afternoon. Left tackle Dion Dawkins and right guard O’Cyrus Torrence played all 57 snaps, while Connor McGovern, Alec Anderson, and Spencer Brown each played 54 (95%). Josh Allen also played 54 snaps before Kyle Allen entered for the final three plays. At running back, James Cook led the group with 35 snaps (61%), followed by Ray Davis with 12 (21%) and Ty Johnson with 10 (18%). Cook made the most of his opportunities, rushing for 157 yards and a touchdown on 18 carries, including a 74-yard scoring run in the fourth quarter. The wide receiver rotation was more evenly distributed. Khalil Shakir led the group with 36 snaps (63%), followed by DJ Moore with 33 (58%), Keon Coleman with 30 (53%), and Skyler Bell with 20 (35%). The tight end usage was particularly interesting. Dawson Knox led the position with 41 snaps (72%), while Jackson Hawes and Dalton Kincaid each played 26 (46%). sports.title: Todd Monken: Getting flexed into Sunday night is really cool for our players
sports.summary: If someone had told you at the beginning of the season that the Week 12 game between the Browns and Raiders would get flexed into Sunday Night Football, you probably would have responded with some healthy skepticism.
sports.body:
But with the way the season has unfolded, that’s exactly what’s happened.

With the Browns at 6-4 and the Raiders at 4-6 — and now starting the league’s No. 1 overall pick at quarterback — the two clubs make for one of the most compelling matchups of Thanksgiving weekend that wasn’t already in a standalone window.

Browns head coach Todd Monken told reporters on Wednesday that getting flexed is “really cool for our players.”

“I said it at the beginning of the year. I mean, you want to be on Thursday Night, Sunday Night, Monday Night — you want to be flexed, means you’re having a good year,” Monken said, via transcript from the team. “As nice as it is to have a one o’clock schedule every week, I mean, I said that, early in the [year]. I mean, you’re on a trajectory to be fired at some point because you’re at one o’clock every week. So, you’re fighting like hell to get to where you’re on national TV. So, if people are going to watch football, and more importantly than that, an opportunity to get to seven [wins].”

Monken also agreed that it’s a good test for the Browns as a young team.

“I think you earn where you’re at in the present moment, and that only lends itself to what’s in front of you and how important that’s going to become,” Monken said. “You know, getting the bye at 6-4 and putting yourself in position where the rest of the games matter, and especially the one coming up.”

This will be the Browns’ first Sunday night game at home since 2019, which should make for a rowdy atmosphere on the shores of Lake Erie.

“Oh, it’s a huge advantage. Huge advantage,” Monken said of the anticipated environment. “Making it hard for the opposing offense, cadence-wise, being able to function, and making an advantage for us when we’re on offense. I mean, it’s a huge advantage, and it should be playing at home.”

sports.title: Ben Johnson sees Bears' 4.2 yards per carry average as "a deceiving statistic"
sports.summary: League wide, NFL teams average 4.2 yards per rushing attempt.
sports.body:
What Johnson does care about is that the running game is efficient, and Johnson would like to see better efficiency than he has seen so far from his offense. Johnson noted that an occasional long run can skew the yards per carry average, and if there are too many runs getting stuffed for no gain, that’s a problem. On the flip side, a one-yard run will bring down any team’s average, but it’s a great play if it happens on fourth-and-goal at the 1-yard line.

“I don’t see it as bigger chunk runs, necessarily. The yards per carry is a deceiving statistic in a lot of ways,” Johnson said. “We run the ball a lot in the red zone, and when you’re down there a four-yard carry is really an explosive.”

Johnson said what he cares more about is efficiency. Many teams look at running success rate, which means the percentage of runs on which a team gains at least 40 percent of yardage needed on first down, at least 60 percent on second down, or at least 100 percent on third or fourth down. The Bears’ success rate this season is 49.2 percent, and Johnson says that’s not good enough.

“We go off efficiency, and we’re under 50 percent efficient running the ball. We set our bar higher than that. We want to be closer to 55 percent, so we’ve got some work to do and all our guys know it,” Johnson said.

Ultimately, Johnson wants to see rushing first downs and rushing touchdowns. Yards per carry is secondary to that.

sports.body: The Buffalo Bills have loved running the football thus far in the 2026 season. James Cook has the second-most carries in the NFL right now at 187. As a team, the Bills are the current owners of the second-highest first-down designed run rate in the NFL at 61.3%. Now, sure, the Bills have recently played in a collection of games that featured plenty of garbage time, when Buffalo has attempted to burn clock by tapping into the run game. Even when garbage-time is considered, the Bills have the NFL’s second-highest run rate on all downs at 45.7%. The rest of the league averages a designed run play on 39.3%. Quarterback scrambles — that occur on dropbacks — and spikes and kneels are excluded in that calculation. Analytics have proven that passing the football is more efficient than running the football. And this article isn’t going to show that the Bills have actually become more efficient on the ground than through the air. Right now, in non-garbage time situations, Buffalo’s designed-run game has provided the team +0.023 EPA per play, the eighth-highest figure in the NFL. The team’s pass game has provided the team +0.239 EPA per dropback, the fourth-best in football. Unsurprisingly, the difference in value added for each method of moving the football has been seismic. Up until now, the Bills have genuinely attempted to “establish” the run in their first nine games of the 2026 campaign. Accepting that fact raises two questions: what type of play call have the Bills chosen on second down and how effective have their second downs been? Before I begin with the results, despite an overall negative EPA in first-down run scenarios (-0.059, the 15th-highest in football), the Bills have had 16.4% of those runs gain 10+ yards. That’s the fourth-best in the NFL and much higher than the league average of 10.3%. This is where things get fascinating for Buffalo’s elite offense. And where it has leaned on its pass game. On second down after a first-down run — in non-garbage time scenarios, of course — the Bills have dropped back to pass 73.8% of the time, which is the fourth-highest rate in the NFL and noticeably higher than the league average of 64.5%. sports.title: Report: Mike Pettine takes over as Cowboys' defensive play-caller
sports.summary: Christian Parker will remain the defensive coordinator.
sports.body:
Via ESPN, Pettine will be taking over as the play-caller for the Dallas Cowboys defense.

Pettine supplants defensive coordinator Christian Parker, a Pettine protege who is in his first year as the coach in charge of an NFL defense. Parker will remain the team’s defensive coordinator.

It was obvious that something was coming. Sunday’s 46-40 loss to the 49ers included an embarrassing performance from the defense, highlighted by multiple players running the wrong way when receiver Deebo Samuel rumbled 70 yards for a rushing touchdown.

Some would say Pettine is part of the problem, given that he has been there for multiple weeks. Short of firing everyone and hiring someone off the street, however, there’s not much that can be done right now.

The first test comes on Sunday, when the Cowboys host the one-win Titans. Four days later, Dallas faces the two-win Eagles. If the Cowboys don’t win both, they’ll likely be de facto done for 2026.

sports.body: The New York Jets have solicited advice from nearly everyone on planet Earth when hiring head coaches this century. That has included The 33rd Team, Charley Casserly, and do you remember that one time when Pro Football Hall of Famer Peyton Manning made a phone call to seal the deal for Adam Gase? Great times. That can’t happen in 2027. Make no mistake about it: the Jets will be looking for a new head coach in a matter of months, but in all of those other situations, they lost the battle before it ever began. Stop relying on people outside of the building. Put your big boy pants on and make a decision for yourself. Who is the right man for that job? Darren Mougey. Woody Johnson has called Mougey “The General” this offseason when referencing him to fans. He has spoken highly of him and believes the team is going in the right direction because of Mougey. Put him in the driver’s seat for this search and allow him to vet the candidates. ESPN New York’s Jake Asman called the latest Jets HC search a “sham” on the “Jets Collective” podcast. “Woody Johnson put Mike Tannenbaum, Rick Spielman, and The 33rd Team in charge of vetting candidates. Liam Coen is a UMass alum, Mike Tannenbaum went to UMass, and again, I work with Mike, so I’m comfortable saying this to his face.
